chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas, from the one who mentioned him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Imam settles the debts of the believers, except for the dowries (mehrs) of the women.

key_terms.إِمَام: The Imam, the divinely appointed leader

ai.seo_question: What debts does the Imam settle for believers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the Imam’s judicial and financial authority to discharge communal debts, reflecting the concept of *Qada’ al-Duyun*. The explicit exclusion of *mehar* (dowry) highlights the preservation of women’s private financial rights (*Haqq al-Nafs*) distinct from public treasury obligations, a principle widely cited in Shia jurisprudence regarding state responsibility for insolvent believers.
